trait: APOE alleles (e2, e3, e4, and the rare e1)
reading: e2/e3: odds of Alzheimer's disease about 0.6 times those of e3/e3.
note: Odds ratios of Alzheimer's disease against e3/e3 from a meta-analysis of clinic and autopsy studies of people of European descent (Farrer 1997), adjusted for age: odds ratios of those case-control studies, not a lifetime risk. The e4 effect was seen at every age from 40 to 90 but was smaller after 70, and the risk of a genotype differed between men and women. The e4 effect was weaker in African American and Hispanic people and stronger in Japanese people. The two sites also make the rare e1, whose pairs are not read. Step 25's Alzheimer's score (PGS000334) includes the same two sites; docs/42-traits.md says why step 06 does not list APOE.

trait: Bitter taste haplotype (TAS2R38, PTC and PROP)
reading: Not read: needs a genotype at every one of rs713598, rs1726866 and rs10246939.
note: The three TAS2R38 sites of the traits table read together: PAV (Pro49, Ala262, Val296) is the taster form and AVI (Ala49, Val262, Ile296) the non-taster form. Kim 2003 found five haplotypes worldwide; this rule reads the two common ones, and a copy with another (AAV, AAI, PVI or a rarer one) is not read. TAS2R38 lies on the minus strand, so the alleles here are the complement of the codon bases.

trait: APOL1 kidney risk variants (G1 read, G2 not read)
reading: Not read: needs a genotype at both rs73885319 and rs60910145.
note: G1 is two missense changes that sit on one copy, S342G (rs73885319) and I384M (rs60910145), in perfect linkage disequilibrium in Genovese 2010, so they are read together without phase. G2 (rs71785313) is a 6-base deletion of N388 and Y389; this rule table reads single-base sites only, so this rule does not read G2 and a G2 copy reads as G0 here; the HTML report reads G2 from the sample's VCF beside this result (og summary collect). G1 and G2 never share a copy. In African Americans, two risk copies (G1 or G2) went with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (odds ratio 10.5) and hypertension-attributed end-stage kidney disease (odds ratio 7.3), and one copy did not raise the risk (a recessive pattern). Both variants are common on African chromosomes and were absent from the European chromosomes studied.

trait: Alpha-1 antitrypsin Pi type (M, S, Z)
reading: Not read: needs a genotype at both rs17580 and rs28929474.
note: The two common deficiency alleles of SERPINA1: S (Glu264Val, rs17580) and Z (Glu342Lys, rs28929474). SERPINA1 lies on the minus strand, so the alleles here are the complement of the codon bases. M stands for a copy with neither S nor Z; other deficiency and null alleles are not read. The readings follow the ATS/ERS 2003 standards; a serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level confirms a deficiency. Z is most common in people of northern European descent.

reading: Not read: needs a genotype at both rs1800562 and rs1799945.
note: The two HFE missense changes of Feder 1996: C282Y (rs1800562), found homozygous in 83% of 178 patients with hereditary haemochromatosis, and H63D (rs1799945). The two sites are about 2 kb apart, too far for most read pairs to phase: heterozygous at both reads as C282Y/H63D, one change on each copy, and the reading says it assumes that. Many people with a risk genotype never build up iron; ferritin and transferrin saturation tell. How many become ill comes from later cohorts: in a Melbourne cohort of people of northern European descent aged 40 to 69, followed for 12 years, iron-overload disease was documented in 28% of male and 1% of female C282Y homozygotes (Allen 2008) and in 1 of 82 male and none of 95 female C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes (Gurrin 2009); a US screening of 41,038 clinic attendees put frank haemochromatosis at under 1% of homozygotes (Beutler 2002). The secondary-findings list reports C282Y homozygotes too (assets/acmg_sf.tsv); this line is the reading of every genotype. C282Y is most common in people of northern European descent.

trait: Vitamin D-binding protein type (Gc1F, Gc1S, Gc2)
reading: Not read: needs a genotype at both rs7041 and rs4588.
note: rs7041 (Asp432Glu) and rs4588 (Thr436Lys) together give the three common vitamin D-binding protein types: Gc1F (Asp, Thr), Gc1S (Glu, Thr) and Gc2 (Asp, Lys). GC lies on the minus strand, so the alleles here are the complement of the codon bases. In Powe 2013 the two sites explained 9.9% of the variation in total 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and Gc1F was the most common type in black participants and Gc1S in white ones. That study also reported protein levels that differed widely by type, but its monoclonal assay reads the types differently: with mass spectrometry or a polyclonal assay, genotype explained at most 9% of the variation in the protein level, against 85% with the monoclonal assay (Denburg 2016). So the readings name the type and give no protein level. A protein type, not a vitamin D deficiency.

reading: Not read: needs a genotype at both rs10757278 and rs1333049.
note: Two tags of the 9p21 risk haplotype near CDKN2A and CDKN2B: rs10757278 (G, Helgadottir 2007, myocardial infarction) and rs1333049 (C, the strongest coronary artery disease signal of the WTCCC 2007 scan). McPherson 2007 found the same interval, with no link to cholesterol, blood pressure or diabetes. The two are read together as tags of one haplotype; heterozygous at both reads as one risk copy, and the reading says it assumes both risk alleles sit on that copy. A copy with only one of the two risk alleles is not read. The studies were of people of European descent.

reading: Not read: needs a genotype at both rs1052553 and rs8070723.
note: The 17q21.31 region around MAPT comes in two lineages, H1 and H2, that differ by a 900-kb inversion and do not recombine (Stefansson 2005); H2 was found in about 20% of European chromosomes, rarely in Africans and almost never in East Asians. Two H1/H2 tags are read together: rs1052553 in MAPT (A is H1, Wider 2010) and rs8070723 (Hoglinger 2011's proxy for H1/H2, its minor allele G in H2). A copy with H1 at one tag and H2 at the other is not read. GRCh38 carries H1.
